description: Weekly physical activity guidance by age band. Aerobic and muscle-strengthening figures are the WHO 2020 recommendations; the Indian age-band restatement is from ICMR-NIN Dietary Guidelines for Indians 2024.

ageBands.label: Children and adolescents (5-17 years)
ageBands.muscleStrengtheningNote: Vigorous-intensity aerobic activity plus activity that strengthens muscle and bone on at least 3 days a week.
ageBands.sedentaryNote: Limit time spent being sedentary, especially recreational screen time.

ageBands.label: Adults (18-64 years)
ageBands.muscleStrengtheningNote: Muscle-strengthening activity at moderate or greater intensity involving all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week.
ageBands.additionalBenefitNote: More than 300 minutes of moderate-intensity, or more than 150 minutes of vigorous-intensity activity per week gives additional health benefits.
ageBands.sedentaryNote: Limit sedentary time. Replacing sedentary time with activity of any intensity, including light intensity, benefits health.

ageBands.label: Older adults (65 years and older)
ageBands.muscleStrengtheningNote: Muscle-strengthening activity at moderate or greater intensity involving all major muscle groups on 2 or more days a week.
ageBands.balanceNote: As part of weekly activity, do varied multicomponent activity emphasising functional balance and strength training at moderate or greater intensity on 3 or more days a week, to improve functional capacity and prevent falls.
ageBands.sedentaryNote: Limit sedentary time. Replacing sedentary time with activity of any intensity benefits health.

medicalClearanceNotes.text: If you follow a sedentary lifestyle it is wise to consult a doctor before starting an exercise programme.
Exercise intensity and duration should be increased gradually. Shortness of breath, pain, nausea, vomiting and headache are warning signs that the body needs rest.
People with illnesses or chronic diseases such as heart disease, high blood pressure, diabetes, asthma, osteoporosis and obesity should consult a physician before taking up an exercise programme.
Men and women over 40 years of age should consult a doctor or healthcare provider before starting a vigorous physical activity programme.
Doing some physical activity is better than doing none. Start with small amounts and gradually increase frequency, intensity and duration.
